title: Illinois 1937
bigQuestion: What did 1937 start in Illinois, if people had wrestled there long before?

story.title: A Program Under a State Seal
story.kicker: A tournament program from 1937 marks a beginning, but not the beginning of wrestling.
paragraphs: Picture a thin paper program from the spring of 1937. At the top is the seal of the Illinois High School Association. Below it are the words State Wrestling Tournament. It is the first one the association ever held.

Inside, the pages are lists. Each list is headed by a weight. Under each weight are names of high school boys and the towns of their schools. Next to the lists are blank lines for scores. Someone at the tournament will fill them in with a pencil.

The paper is new in 1937. Wrestling in Illinois is not. More than a hundred years earlier, a young Abraham Lincoln wrestled in the village of New Salem. In 1908, crowds in Chicago watched a famous professional match.
So what does the program mark? It marks the day wrestling became a state school sport with a champion in each weight. That is a real change. It is just not the first time anyone in Illinois wrestled.
story.think: What is the difference between the first state champion and the first person to wrestle?

lessons.title: What the IHSA Is
lessons.mainIdea: The Illinois High School Association, founded in 1900, runs state contests for Illinois high schools.
reading: The *IHSA* is the Illinois High School Association. It was founded in 1900. Member high schools agreed to follow shared rules for school contests. Before that, each school or town could set its own rules.
An *association* is a group of members who agree to work under the same rules. The IHSA decides who may play, which rules apply and how state tournaments are run. It also crowns state champions.

The IHSA did not start with wrestling. Its first state contests were in other sports. For example, boys tennis crowned its first state champion in 1912. Each sport joined the state series in its own year.

words.d: the Illinois High School Association, founded in 1900, which runs state high school contests
a group of members who agree to work under the same rules

lessons.title: The First State Champions
lessons.mainIdea: In 1937, the IHSA crowned its first state wrestling champions, one in each weight class.
reading: In 1937, the IHSA held its first state wrestling tournament for boys. It named a *state champion* in each weight class. A state champion is the winner of the last round of the state tournament.
The tournament used a *bracket*. A bracket is a chart that shows who meets whom in each round. Winners move to the next line. The last two wrestlers in each weight meet for the title.

The IHSA keeps lists of state champions in its records. Those lists begin with 1937 for wrestling. That is why historians of Illinois school sports use 1937 as the start date. It is a date for a school contest, not for a practice.

words.d: the winner of the final round of a state tournament
a chart showing who meets whom in each round of a tournament

lessons.title: A Rule Book for Many States
lessons.mainIdea: State associations share rule books through a national federation, the NFHS.
reading: Illinois is not the only state with a high school association. Every state has one. In 1920, a few Midwest state associations formed a national group. Today it is the *National Federation of State High School Associations*, or NFHS.

The NFHS writes rule books for many school sports, including wrestling. State groups like the IHSA use those books. That way, a wrestling match in Illinois follows nearly the same rules as one in Ohio.

A shared rule book is a *standard*. A standard is a rule many groups agree to use. Standards let schools from different towns meet fairly. They also let a record in one state be compared with a record in another.

words.w: National Federation of State High School Associations
words.d: the NFHS, formed in 1920, which writes rule books used by state high school groups
a rule that many groups agree to use the same way

lessons.title: Lincoln at New Salem
lessons.mainIdea: Abraham Lincoln wrestled at New Salem, Illinois, around 1831, more than a century before the first state tournament.
reading: In 1831, young Abraham Lincoln moved to *New Salem*, a small village on the Sangamon River in Illinois. He worked in a store. In frontier villages, wrestling was a common way for young men to test strength and win respect.

Stories say Lincoln wrestled Jack Armstrong, leader of a local group called the Clary's Grove boys. People who knew Lincoln told different versions later. Some said it ended in a draw. All agree that Lincoln earned the group's respect.

Many stories about Lincoln's wrestling were told after he became famous. Historians treat the details carefully. Still, the National Wrestling Hall of Fame honors Lincoln. The New Salem village has been rebuilt as a state historic site near Petersburg.

words.d: a village on the Sangamon River in Illinois where Lincoln lived in the 1830s
the edge of settled land in the early United States, where towns were new and small

lessons.title: A Famous Match in Chicago
lessons.mainIdea: In 1908 and 1911, Frank Gotch and George Hackenschmidt drew huge crowds to professional matches in Chicago.
reading: *Professional* wrestlers wrestle for money. In the early 1900s, one of the most famous was Frank Gotch. He was a farm boy from Humboldt, Iowa. His great rival was George Hackenschmidt, a strongman born in Estonia, then part of the Russian Empire.

In April 1908, Gotch and Hackenschmidt met at the Dexter Park Pavilion in Chicago. The pavilion stood near the city's Union Stock Yards. Gotch won and was called world heavyweight champion. Newspapers across the country reported the result.

They met again in Chicago on Labor Day in 1911. This time the match was at Comiskey Park, the White Sox ballpark. A very large crowd came. Gotch won again. These matches show that Chicago was a wrestling city decades before 1937.

words.d: doing something as a paid job; professional wrestlers wrestle for money
a person someone competes against again and again

lessons.title: Clubs and Colleges
lessons.mainIdea: Amateur clubs and colleges held wrestling championships before Illinois high schools did.
reading: An *amateur* competes without being paid. In 1888, clubs across the United States formed the Amateur Athletic Union, or AAU. The AAU held national championships in many sports, including wrestling. Athletes from city athletic clubs entered.

Colleges also had wrestling teams. The National Collegiate Athletic Association, the *NCAA*, held its first national wrestling championships in 1928. College matches followed their own rule book, a little different from high school rules.

So by 1937, Illinois wrestlers could already compete in clubs, colleges and professional shows. The IHSA tournament added one more room: the high school. Each room had its own leaders, rule book and champions.

words.d: a person who competes without being paid
the National Collegiate Athletic Association, which runs college sports championships

lessons.title: A First Title, Not a First Hold
lessons.mainIdea: The year 1937 marks the start of a school contest, not the start of wrestling.
reading: Historians ask what a date measures. The year 1937 measures when the IHSA first crowned wrestling champions. It does not measure when people first wrestled. For that, we look at *artifacts* like the Beni Hasan tomb paintings, about 4,000 years old.
It helps to line dates up. Beni Hasan is about 4,000 years old. Wrestling joined the ancient Olympics in 708 BCE. Lincoln wrestled at New Salem around 1831. The IHSA tournament came in 1937.
Each of these dates is true. Each answers a different question. Mixing them up is a common mistake. A careful reader always asks: first what, and in which *institution*?

words.d: an object made by people long ago, like a painting or a tool
a lasting group with its own rules, like a school, league or association

check.why: 1937 is the year of the first IHSA state wrestling champions.

check.q: Which is the best question to ask about any 'first' date?

lessons.title: Girls Join the State Finals
lessons.mainIdea: Illinois girls wrestling held its first IHSA state finals in 2022, eighty-five years after the boys.
reading: For most of IHSA history, the state wrestling tournament was for boys only. Some girls wrestled on boys teams over the years. But there was no separate girls state title in Illinois.

That changed in the 2021–22 school year. The IHSA held its first girls wrestling *state finals* in 2022. Girls now had their own weight classes and their own champions. Other states had started girls tournaments too.

The gap between 1937 and 2022 is eighty-five years. That gap shows that a sport can exist long before everyone is let into its *championship*. Dates of new doors are part of history, just like dates of first titles.

words.d: the last rounds of a state tournament, where champions are decided
a contest that decides the official winner of a sport or event

lessons.title: Reading a Tournament Record
lessons.mainIdea: Programs, newspapers and association lists are sources, and each shows something different.
reading: A *primary source* is a record made at the time of an event. A 1937 program is one. A newspaper story from the next morning is another. Historians use primary sources to check what happened.

Each source shows something different. A program printed before a meet lists who entered. A newspaper report tells who won and how many people came. An IHSA champions list gives the names that the association made official.

Sometimes sources disagree about a spelling or a score. Then historians compare them. A careful *record* keeps the name, the school, the weight and the year together. Good records let people today find the wrestlers of 1937.

words.d: a record made at the time of an event, like a program or a newspaper
a written list or account that keeps facts for later
